title: Shared state and checkpoints
summary: Executors share data through workflow state and survive restarts through checkpoints written at the end of each superstep. A checkpoint holds executor state, pending messages, pending requests and shared state, and is a trust boundary.
useIf: A workflow is long, must resume after a failure or pause, or needs audit snapshots.
avoidIf: The workflow finishes in seconds and a rerun is cheaper than storing and securing checkpoints.

explain.md: **Shared state.** Python: `ctx.set_state(key, value)` and `ctx.get_state(key)`. .NET: `QueueStateUpdateAsync` and `ReadStateAsync` with an optional `scopeName` (null means the executor's private scope; a shared name makes it visible to executors using the same name). The writer sees its own update at once; other executors see it in the **next superstep** [[tr17]]. Pass ids through messages and keep big payloads in state.

**Checkpoints** are created at the end of each superstep and capture executor state, pending messages for the next superstep, pending requests and responses, and shared state. Python 1.13.0 (2026-07-30) also writes an entry checkpoint before the first superstep and when request responses arrive, a minor breaking change for code that depends on checkpoint counts or order [[tr18]]. **Resume**: Python `workflow.run(checkpoint_id=..., checkpoint_storage=...)`; .NET `ResumeStreamingAsync(workflow, checkpoint, checkpointManager)` or `run.RestoreCheckpointAsync`. Executors with their own fields save them in `on_checkpoint_save` / `on_checkpoint_restore` (Python) or `OnCheckpointingAsync` / `OnCheckpointRestoredAsync` (.NET) [[tr18]].

async with (
    DefaultAzureCredential() as cred,
    CosmosCheckpointStorage(
        endpoint='https://<acct>.documents.azure.com:443/', credential=cred,
        database_name='agent-framework', container_name='workflow-checkpoints',
        allowed_checkpoint_types=['my_app.models:Ticket'],
    ) as storage,
):
    wf = WorkflowBuilder(start_executor=start, checkpoint_storage=storage)\
        .add_edge(start, step_b).build()
    async for e in wf.run(payload, stream=True): ...
    cps = await storage.list_checkpoints(workflow_name=wf.name)

    # later, new process, rebuilt graph with the same executor ids
    async for e in new_wf.run(checkpoint_id=cps[-1].checkpoint_id,
                              checkpoint_storage=storage, stream=True): ...

explain.title: Checkpoint storage is a code-execution trust boundary
explain.md: File, Cosmos and Foundry stores serialize non-JSON state with `pickle` behind a restricted unpickler by default (File since python-1.0.1, 2026-04-09; Cosmos since python-1.1.0, 2026-04-21). Allow more types with `allowed_checkpoint_types=['module:qualname']` (types only, not functions). Never load checkpoints from untrusted or tampered sources; if pickle is unacceptable use in-memory storage or a custom store [[tr18]].

whereToUse: Long pipelines where a worker can die mid-run
Human approval steps that may wait hours: pending requests are stored and re-emitted on restore
Compliance workflows that keep a snapshot after each step for audit
Moving a run between environments or instances

use: Losing progress would be costly in time, tokens or side effects
You can keep topology and executor ids stable between runs and deploys
The storage backend is private infrastructure with controlled access
avoid: Short, cheap workflows where a rerun is acceptable
Untrusted storage or multi-tenant buckets without strict access control
Side effects that are not idempotent: resume may repeat work after the last checkpoint
flips: Resume must work across processes: move from file to Cosmos or a custom store
Pickle is not allowed by policy: use in-memory storage (no durability) or write a custom serializer, or use the Durable Extension

pitfalls.symptom: Resume fails or the graph restarts from the beginning
pitfalls.cause: The rebuilt workflow has a different topology or executor identities; in .NET agents without a stable `ChatClientAgentOptions.Id` (and unchanged `Name`) get new executor ids
pitfalls.fix: Give every agent a fixed logical id, keep names unchanged, never use user or request ids as agent ids

pitfalls.symptom: Old checkpoints fail to load after an upgrade
pitfalls.cause: Restricted unpickler since 2026-04: custom classes are rejected until allowed
pitfalls.fix: List types in `allowed_checkpoint_types` or `register_checkpoint_type`, or start a new checkpoint lineage

pitfalls.symptom: A test asserting checkpoint counts broke on Python 1.13.0
pitfalls.cause: Entry checkpoints are written before the first superstep and on response delivery since Python 1.13.0 (2026-07-30)
pitfalls.fix: Assert on content and resumability, not on counts or order

scenarios.title: Nightly pipeline on a fleet of workers
scenarios.situation: A batch workflow takes 90 minutes and runs on whichever worker picks it up. A worker is evicted about once a week. Re-running costs about 20 in model tokens.
unknowns: Is pickle allowed by security policy?
scenarios.question: Which checkpoint storage do you choose?

options.name: `CosmosCheckpointStorage` with managed identity, scoped container and an explicit `allowed_checkpoint_types`
options.why: Cross-process and durable, RBAC-controlled, and unpickling is restricted to listed types.
options.tradeoff: Beta package, request units to provision, and the container is a trust boundary you must lock down.

options.name: `FileCheckpointStorage` on a local disk
options.why: A replacement worker cannot see the evicted worker's disk.
options.tradeoff: Fine on one machine for development.

options.name: `InMemoryCheckpointStorage`
options.why: Lost with the process, so it gives no recovery.
options.tradeoff: Right for tests and when pickle is forbidden and reruns are cheap.

flips.then: Write a custom `CheckpointStorage` with JSON-only state or move to the Durable Extension.
Skip checkpoints and make steps idempotent.

scenarios.takeaway: Pick storage by who must read the checkpoint: the same process, the same machine or any worker.

scenarios.title: Sensitive-data workflow with audit
scenarios.situation: A workflow processes health claims. Auditors want a snapshot per step. Checkpoints would contain claim text. The security team rejects shared storage accounts.
unknowns: Is encryption at rest with customer keys required?
Are payloads needed in checkpoints or can they be ids?
scenarios.question: What is your approach?

options.name: Keep payloads out of messages and state (store ids, fetch from the system of record), use a private checkpoint store with RBAC and encryption, restrict allowed types
options.why: Checkpoints hold only references, the store is private, and unpickling is restricted.
options.tradeoff: Extra fetches per step and design discipline.

options.name: Checkpoint everything to a shared file share
options.why: Sensitive content in a broadly readable store, and a writable store is a code-execution risk.

options.name: Disable checkpointing
options.tradeoff: No resume and no per-step audit snapshots.

flips.then: Use encrypted storage with customer-managed keys and strict retention.

flips.if: Runs are short and reruns are safe

scenarios.takeaway: Checkpoint what you can afford to leak, and lock down the rest.

quiz.q: After redeploying a .NET service, resuming a checkpoint fails. The workflow contains local `ChatClientAgent` instances created without options ids. What is the likely cause?
options: Checkpoints cannot be resumed after deploy
Executor identities no longer match because the agents lack stable `ChatClientAgentOptions.Id` values
quiz.explain: A rehydrated workflow must keep topology and executor identities. Assign stable ids (and keep `Name` unchanged) to each agent.

quiz.q: Which are true about Python file and Cosmos checkpoint security? Select all.
options: Non-JSON state is serialized with pickle behind a restricted unpickler by default
`allowed_checkpoint_types` entries must resolve to types, not functions
Loading checkpoints from tampered storage is safe because of the restricted unpickler
`InMemoryCheckpointStorage` avoids pickle but is not durable
quiz.explain: The docs call checkpoint storage a trust boundary: never load from untrusted or tampered sources, even with the restricted unpickler.

quiz.q: When does another executor see a state value written in a superstep?
options: In the next superstep, while the writer sees it at once
quiz.explain: Visibility follows superstep rules: the writer reads its own update in the same handler, others from the next superstep.

flashcards.back: Executor state, pending messages for the next superstep, pending requests and responses, and shared state. Created at the end of each superstep.

flashcards.front: What must stay the same for a rebuilt workflow to resume?
flashcards.back: Topology and executor identities. In .NET give agents a stable `ChatClientAgentOptions.Id` and keep `Name` unchanged.

flashcards.front: Which Python checkpoint stores use pickle?
flashcards.back: File, Cosmos and Foundry stores, behind a restricted unpickler. Extend with `allowed_checkpoint_types=['module:qualname']`.
